pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 13.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: VISUALISING AND SUMMARISING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.2: Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Which words or expressions appeal to the five senses?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify mental images created from a read passage

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify mental images created from a read passage
   In simple words: practise until you can identify mental images created from a read passage. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising.
4. Show that you can: identify mental images created from a read passage

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visualising and Summarising important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Search from print and electronic sources and list down the sensory words and expressions used to create mental images in a text,
2. Read a passage on an interesting issue like sea travel and, jointly, pick out the sensory words or expressions and the mental images they create in a reader,
3. In groups, fill in templates requiring key ideas from the text or parts of the text and display the templates on the wall,
4. Read a text on current issues such as responsible sea travel and identify the main ideas in a paragraph or a passage,

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words or expressions appeal to the five senses?
2. Why is it important to make a relevant summary of a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify mental images created from a read passage

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
